The Scheduled Above
Civic-ceremonial centers were highly
structured spaces for public
politico-religious rituals, meant to
inculcate the masses.
The Secret Below
Natural caves were hidden, intimate
realms where elites and non-elites alike
communed with deities, conducted
funerary rites, and petitioned for rain.

The Macal River Valley
Defined by steep,
densely vegetated
peaks, steep-sided
canyons, and a
massive network of
karstic caves that
served as a major
artery linking the
Caribbean coast and
the central Lowlands.

The Teotihuacan
Revival
The Text: Simplified Maya ajaw
("king") glyphs.
• The Motif: The "Mexican Year Sign" _the distinctive emblem
of the headdresses of Teotihuacan rulers.
Dating to the Late Classic (after Teotihuacan's collapse), this vase represents a "revivalist movement" where
distant Maya elites adopted ancient central Mexican power symbols to legitimize their own authority.

Surviving the Humidity
Finding intact carved wood in the humid tropical
lowlands of the Maya area is an extreme rarity, making
this fragmentary artifact a miraculous survival.

The Light in the Dark
Isolated artifacts tell us about the hands that
painted them. Artifacts left in situ tell us
about the minds that placed them.
The Macal River Valley caves prove that true archaeological value lies not in the beauty of the
objects, but in their deliberate, undisturbed placement in the dark-a context that, once
looted, can never be restored.
